page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-80 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n2d family. It features 80 vCPUs mapped to 40 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The CPU allocation is dedicated, with hyperthreading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The instance is configured with 80.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 107952.86 and single-core scoring 2693.85, both placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Passmark CPU tests also show strong capabilities, with a CPU score of 69646.99 and strong performance in extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Memory performance is mixed; cached small-block read bandwidth is strong at 5077.68 GB/sec, and large-block write bandwidth is strong at 109.12 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read bandwidth is average at 187.06 GB/sec.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the n2d-highcpu-80 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:1, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory processing. However, it demonstrates strong performance in database operations with 25376.0 on Passmark and Redis SET operations at 77.49 million operations per second. It is also highly capable in software compilation, with a strong Geekbench clang compilation score of 43413.0, and ray tracing at 70957.0. This makes the instance well-suited for compute-heavy workloads such as software build pipelines, parallel processing, web serving, and moderate database operations that do not require massive memory footprints.
